Did it really bomb? I have the original Wii and was considering getting the Wii U but I don't know if it would be worth it.

Since its launch in late 2012, Nintendo has probably sold around 9.5 million units of the Wii U. Comparing it to the sales of the PS4 (22 million), the Xbone (10 million), the Wii (101 million), the Wii three years after release (67 million), and the GameCube three years after release (probably around 11 million), the Wii U has not sold very well for Nintendo. It's definitely doing better than previously, but it's probably going to sell worse than the GameCube (21 million) by the end of the Wii U's lifespan.

Maybe not the worst, but Nokia moving to Windows Phone has to be up there.

With the "Burning Platform" memo, they discouraged customers from buying their existing Symbian and MeeGo devices. It took Nokia almost a year to release their first Windows Phone, and by that time sales had heavily declined. Furthermore, there wasn't great demand for Windows Phone, so they started losing money heavily on their iconic mobile phone business. This led the once largest mobile phone manufacturer to drop out of the mobile phone business.
Nokia was purchased by Microsoft. A certain division anyways.

After the acquisition by Microsoft, 18,000 people were laid off in Nokia's devices and services business in 2014. Now another 7,800 are going to be let go. Most are in the windows phone business. Spending 7.6 billion on Nokia's phone business was Steve Ballmer's idea.

Source: money.cnn

Absolutely spot on. A single memo destroyed 2-3% of Finnish GDP. Has gotta be one Godzilla of a memo. It indeed WAS at that time, as a long time Nokia fan, I was utterly appalled at that memo, most Nokia fans knew instantly that Redmond was up to some mischief and were scuttling Nokia so that Microsoft could float their own boat. Fast forward to just a few days back, our fears came true, Microsoft couldn't do squat with Nokia's hardware division - it's a total write off.

Now, we don't know for sure how Nokia would've fared if they had continued with symbian and its successor Meego. Since Nokia worked like a government, they had many groups within the company that would have read the writing on the wall and fared better than a Microsoft takeover. As an example the Nokia android tablet turned out just fine, sadly, Nokia lost their mojo by then.
